subject: Sizing recommendation and hot-standby bridge for Solaris renewal
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@solaris.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing recommendation and hot-standby bridge for Solaris renewal

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. I pulled together an initial sizing recommendation based on the last six weeks of observed usage and the Q1 burst patterns you shared. Key points up front:

- Current steady-state utilization across your model mix averages ~62% of your committed H100 pool during business hours, but spikes to 135% for short windows tied to nightly batch scoring.
- We recommend a modest committed increase of +8 H100-equivalent slots to cover predictable growth and to lower per-token unit cost.
- To avoid a hard capacity outage during the renewal lead time, propose a 90-day hot-standby bridge (burst capacity on reserved hardware) that gives you 160% of baseline for peak windows while we onboard the tranche.

I've attached the usage export (solar_usage_apr_q1.csv) and a draft SOW (proposed_sow_solaris_v1.2.pdf) with the proposed phasing and pricing. Can you confirm:

1) Does procurement need an itemized PO-friendly SOW or will the draft suffice?
2) Any constraints on region/firmware for the H100 hardware (we can pin to a specific AZ)?

If useful I can loop in Karthik (infrastructure) and Ben (solutions) to validate the bridge sizing and the suggested autoscale floor.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia —

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers and a couple of asks:

- Procurement will want an itemized SOW we can attach to the PO; pricing lines need to show committed tranche and the bridge as a separate monthly SKU.
- We prefer the us-west-2 region (latency to our customers).
- Can you justify the +8 H100 figure with the 95th percentile tail? Last renewal we saw unaccounted tails that drove overages.

I'll schedule a brief sync with procurement on Thursday afternoon. If Karthik or Ben can join to walk the technical side that would be great.

Subject: Re: Sizing recommendation and hot-standby bridge for Solaris renewal

Forwarding my quick run on the usage export — I pulled the 95th and 99th percentile concurrency across the last eight weeks. Short summary:

- 95th percentile concurrency aligns with +6 H100 slots above steady-state; 99th percentile pushes to +12 for <30 minute windows.
- The burst pattern is almost exclusively nightly batch scoring (02:00–04:00 UTC) and a few marketing-driven spikes.
- Bridge sizing: target +10 H100 for bridge pool to ensure we don't exceed capacity during 99th spikes while the tranche is provisioning. We can tune autoscale floor to 50% of bridge to save cost during low nights.

Notes for SOW: we should call out the ability to ephemeralize the bridge when steady state stabilizes, with a defined rollback cadence (30/60/90 days). Also recommend including a data retention clause for debug logs (30 days).

—Karthik
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

Alex —

I'll join the Thursday call and can walk the operational trade-offs. A couple specifics I'll bring:

- Pricing model: committed tranche priced by H100-equivalent slot-month; bridge priced as a short-term reserved SKU at a premium (we show both monthly and daily billing options in the SOW).
- Observability: we will provision a per-route latency and token-cost dashboard for Solaris so you can prove cost-savings once the tranche is live.
- Fallbacks: we propose automatic fallback to a slightly lower-precision quantized variant for non-critical batch scoring if the bridge hits capacity unexpectedly — this preserves throughput while saving tokens.
